first.rationale: The two declining metrics (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) are plausibly linked, and onboarding sits upstream of activation, so fixing it is the intervention most likely to move both without buying revenue. memory_86 and memory_31 are the load-bearing support for that choice, so they are the first two verification pulls: both are compressed claims stripped of effect size, duration, segment, and follow-up window, and 'durable lift in first-week activation' measured at day 12 may simply not have been observed long enough to be durable. I specifically want the archive to tell me whether the original onboarding/signup wins were measured on activation alone or carried through to retained, qualified revenue — cutting required signup fields can raise activation while degrading lead qualification data and downstream sales conversion, which would be a real cost against the primary objective. That is the downstream value risk I am flagging. The third pull is memory_73 because competitive price pressure makes promotional pricing the tempting reflex, and it is the option with the worst asymmetry: a discount response to a competitor's entry pricing can show strong acquisition and revenue lift in-window while importing price-sensitive, low-retention accounts and resetting price expectations for the segment. I want to see whether the original record tracked cohort retention past the promo period before I let that memory pull the slot. Note also that these memories were consolidated as isolated wins under earlier market conditions; none of them were run against an active competitor undercutting the SMB segment, so their transfer to day 76 is an assumption, not a finding. If verification shows the onboarding results were short-window or activation-only, I will fall back to activation_messaging (memory_91, the most recent record at day 61 and closest to the larger decline) rather than to pricing. I am scoping this as a standard experiment on the self-serve SMB funnel only, holding the enterprise demo-request path out per memory_44, with explicit guardrails on lead quality, sales-accepted rate, and 30/60-day retention — not just completion rate — so the experiment can actually detect the failure mode I am worried about.

final.rationale:
Verification changed the picture in one important way and confirmed the plan in another. The critical finding is memory_73: the consolidated note said 'effective response for price-sensitive SMB, strong acquisition and revenue lift' and omitted 30-day retention -12% plus an explicit source-record instruction not to generalize targeted discounting as sustainable growth. The inherited summary had been stripped of exactly the evidence that reverses the decision. Under a primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, promotional pricing is now affirmatively ruled out as the competitive response, not merely deprioritized — the +18% qualified revenue is an in-window artifact of a cohort that does not survive first renewal. That also forces a general downgrade of trust in the three memories I could not afford to verify (memory_57, memory_44, memory_91): they are the same compression format from the same pipeline, so I should assume they too may have lost their caveats and negative results, and I will not treat them as load-bearing.

exp_86 confirms simplify_onboarding: completion +13%, time-to-value -2.1 days, and importantly 30-day retention +3%, so the lift is not being bought at the cost of cohort quality. This is the only verified direction that improves a leading metric and retention together, and onboarding sits upstream of activation, so it is the intervention most likely to address both the -4% completion and the -6% activation decline at their common root. exp_31 supports the adjacent signup-field change but is weaker and I am treating it as secondary: activation +9% came with retention -1% and only +4% qualified revenue, and it explicitly did not replicate outside SMB. So I am running the onboarding-flow shortening as the primary lever and holding aggressive signup-field cuts as a contained sub-arm at most, because reducing required fields is the specific mechanism that can degrade lead qualification data and downstream sales conversion.

Remaining uncertainty I am not papering over: exp_86 reported completion, time-to-value, and retention but no qualified revenue figure, so its link to the actual objective is inferred rather than measured. None of these experiments were run against an active competitor undercutting the SMB segment, so transfer to day 76 conditions is an assumption. Scope is the self-serve SMB funnel with the enterprise demo-request path held out per memory_44, and I will instrument sales-accepted lead rate, first-renewal retention, and qualified revenue per cohort — not completion rate alone — with a pre-set stop if lead quality or retention degrades, since that is precisely the failure mode the archive shows a consolidated memory can hide. Recommend the source records for memory_57, memory_44, and memory_91 be pulled next cycle before any of them is acted on.
